LAN wins explanation
The "LAN win" component of the VRS finds the 10 most recent LAN wins. There is only one factor involved:
  • Recency: A win counts for 100% if it is within the last month. From there and 5 months back a match will lose its value down to zero.

Opponent network explanation
The "opponent network" component of the VRS finds the 10 best wins by 3 different factors:
  • Opponent network: The value of a win depends on the opponents' network. The opponent network represent how many different teams a team has won against recently. The factor is a value between zero and one, where 1 means the team is amongst the most valuable teams to beat.
  • Recency: A win counts for 100% if it is within the last month. From there and 5 months back a match will lose its value down to zero.
  • Event value: A win will be worth more if it is won in a valuable event, in regards to prize pool.

Bounty offered explanation

  • Prize won: The more money you win, the better

Head to head explanation
The "Head to head" component of the VRS is a bit different from the other 4 components. First the other 4 components are calculated and all teams get a ranking starting point. Then the head to head calculation will go through all matches from oldest to newest. It will move points from the loser to the winner. The amount of points will be based on:
  • The two teams' ranking: If a team with a low ranking beat a team with a high ranking, they will earn many points. And on the other hand: if a team with a high ranking beat a team with a low ranking they will only gain little points.
  • Recency: The longer time since the match was player the fewer points will be moved.
Note that the "Head to head" component is recalculated every time the ranking is calculated. This means that if you have beaten an opponent for 3 months ago, and they since then have improved their ranking - your wins will be worth more.
